question: Can exact feature redundancy in a trained neural network be formalized as natural isomorphisms, summarized by an intrinsic layer-wise feature-complexity measure, and exploited by a data-free, no-fine-tuning weight-merging algorithm?

key_findings.claim: The paper proposes a categorical language for functional feature equivalence and defines layer-wise feature complexity as the width of a purported feature poset.
key_findings.evidence: A network architecture is represented as a category, a concrete parameterization as a functor, and an invertible natural transformation between two parameterized functors as functional equivalence. For one network, non-identity natural automorphisms are then linked to redundant features, and the maximum number of mutually non-equivalent features is called feature complexity. This is an appealing organizing vocabulary, but the source and target categories, their morphism equalities, and the feature order are not specified rigorously enough to make the construction independently checkable.

anchors.section: 3.1 Category Theory View of Neural Networks

key_findings.claim: Proposition 3.2, the central assertion that linear mode connectivity implies a natural isomorphism and hence functionally equivalent features, is not proved and is false at the stated level of generality.
key_findings.evidence: LMC is defined only as approximate equality of a scalar dataset loss along a parameter segment, whereas natural isomorphism is an exact layer-wise commutation property. The proof immediately invokes Eq. 12, which is the separate, strictly stronger LLFC definition, not a consequence of LMC; the cited LLFC paper reports empirical near-co-occurrence rather than a universal implication. Even granting exact LLFC, the linear-layer expansion yields only (W_a-W_b)(Z_a-Z_b)=0. The manuscript then asserts W_b Z_b = W_a Z_b, which would additionally require (W_a-W_b)Z_b=0 and does not follow. Thus neither LMC nor the displayed algebra establishes naturality.

key_findings.claim: Theorem 3.3 does not establish the claimed equivalence between duplicate features and multiple natural automorphisms, so the theoretical basis of the feature-complexity metric remains unsupported.
key_findings.evidence: The relation Z_i <= Z_j is introduced through an undefined 'simple transformation' and is never shown to be reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. The text simultaneously says comparable features are equal, which would require quotienting duplicate indices before obtaining a poset. Appendix B.2 argues only from an assumed non-identity natural isomorphism toward equality, uses an invalid maximal-chain step, and never constructs the converse natural automorphism from two equal feature maps. Equality on realized data also need not imply that a neuron permutation commutes with all adjacent layer maps, especially when outgoing weights differ.

key_findings.claim: Iterative Feature Merging is a useful weight-space compression heuristic, but it does not measure or identify the paper's formally defined functional equivalence.
key_findings.evidence: IFM ranks pairs by the Euclidean distance between their incoming rows and outgoing columns and stops when the smallest distance exceeds beta times the largest. No theorem connects this relative weight distance to a natural transformation, duplicate feature functions, approximation error, or the width of the proposed poset. Exactly identical activations can have different outgoing weights and remain losslessly mergeable, yet Eq. 6 penalizes those outgoing differences; conversely, close weights need not yield equivalent activations under normalization, biases, nonlinearities, or distribution shift.

anchors.section: 4 Feature Weight Matching and Feature Merging
Iterative Feature Merging with Weight Matching

key_findings.claim: The stated merge rule and pseudocode are not architecture-agnostic or fully executable as written.
key_findings.evidence: Summing incoming weights and averaging outgoing weights preserves a duplicated pair only under restrictive algebra such as identical affine features with correctly combined biases and a positively homogeneous activation. The method explicitly ignores activation and normalization layers, gives no bias, batch-normalization, residual-branch, grouped-convolution, or attention rule, and later handles ResNet by merging only its last two blocks. Algorithm 1 also loops through l=L while reading W_(l+1), resets every cluster count N_m to one inside each while iteration, and does not show the weight/dimension updates after a merge, conflicting with the weighted-average mechanism in Eq. 10.

key_findings.claim: On CIFAR-10, IFM demonstrates substantial post-training compression without fine-tuning, but the headline operating point is selected using the test set and incurs a material accuracy loss.
key_findings.evidence: For VGG16, the reported model retains 23.03% of parameters and reaches 91.78% test accuracy versus 93.51% before merging, a 1.73-point loss. Figure 2(b) explicitly grid-searches beta and selects the largest value whose test accuracy remains above 95% of the original test accuracy. The resulting curve supports a compression-quality tradeoff, not exact function preservation, and test-based hyperparameter selection biases the reported operating point.

anchors.section: C Details for Iterative Feature Merging

key_findings.claim: The ImageNet results show only modest redundancy under IFM and do not isolate feature complexity as the cause of performance differences.
key_findings.evidence: The paper reports approximately 5% parameter reduction for VGG and 10% for ResNet50 on ImageNet. Its evidence that a same-architecture network with greater feature complexity performs better compares only torchvision ResNet50 V1 and V2 checkpoints: V2 has 80.86% versus 76.13% top-1 and degrades faster under merging, but the checkpoints use different training hyperparameters. Data recipe, regularization, calibration, and weight scale therefore confound the inferred complexity-performance relationship.

key_findings.claim: The broad claim that IFM is the first data-agnostic pruning method needing neither training manipulation nor fine-tuning is contradicted by prior work and by the paper's own evaluation protocol.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript cites Srinivas and Babu's 2015 'Data-free parameter pruning for Deep Neural Networks,' which removes redundant neurons from trained networks without training data, yet omits it from Table 1 and still claims priority. IFM execution is weight-only, but its reported beta is chosen from ten values using test accuracy, so the demonstrated model-selection workflow is not data-free. The comparison to INN covers only ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 and does not establish priority or general dominance.

anchors.section: 5.2.3 The Potential of IFM for Pruning

key_findings.claim: The experiments establish that nearby channels can often be merged with limited in-distribution damage, but they do not establish widespread exact functional equivalence.
key_findings.evidence: The VGG16 heatmap reports a minimum normalized distance of 2e-15 and says most pairwise distances are relatively low without defining a statistical threshold. Interpolating between one model and a permutation chosen from low-distance features preserves CIFAR-10 test accuracy better than random permutations, but this is an approximate, task-level test on a model and its own reindexing. It neither tests exact equality over inputs nor compares independently trained networks as Proposition 3.2 does.

anchors.section: 5.1 Verifying the Existence of Equivalent Features

key_findings.claim: The layer-profile and semantic findings are exploratory visual observations rather than validated properties of feature complexity.
key_findings.evidence: The increase-then-decrease profile is shown for VGGs on CIFAR-10 with no normalization for layer width, threshold sensitivity analysis, seeds, uncertainty, or alternative complexity measures. The semantic interpretation uses selected guided-backpropagation images of trucks, legs, and boats; there is no annotation protocol, random-group control, faithfulness test, or quantitative semantic consistency score. Guided visualization can therefore support hypotheses, but not the stated general conclusions.

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence lacks the uncertainty, resource, and breadth needed to support architecture-agnostic compression or intrinsic-complexity claims.
key_findings.evidence: CIFAR models appear as single training runs; accuracy curves have no seed intervals or paired tests. ImageNet uses a few torchvision checkpoints rather than multiple initializations. Only image classification, VGG, and partially handled ResNet are evaluated. The efficiency appendix reports only the time for one IFM iteration on one RTX 2080Ti, not total compression time, inference latency, FLOPs, memory traffic, or realized hardware speedup; parameter count is therefore the sole deployment proxy.

method.core_idea: Treat a network architecture as a category and a trained parameterization as a functor, call layer representations functionally equivalent when an invertible natural transformation makes the layer maps commute, define feature complexity from automorphisms of one such functor, and approximate that complexity by greedily merging weight-near channels.
method.mechanism: For each hidden layer, IFM computes a pair distance by adding the Euclidean distance between incoming weight rows and the distance between outgoing weight columns. It repeatedly selects the closest pair, replaces their incoming row by a sum and their outgoing column by a cluster-size-weighted mean, and stops when the minimum distance exceeds a beta fraction of the layer's maximum pair distance. The resulting narrower network is evaluated directly, without fine-tuning, and beta controls the compression-accuracy tradeoff.
assumptions: The proposed architecture and parameter categories are well-defined and naturality evaluated on feature maps captures the intended functional equivalence.
Approximate equality of scalar loss along a parameter segment is sufficient to infer exact layer-wise commutation.
LMC entails LLFC rather than merely co-occurring empirically in selected settings.
A natural automorphism exists exactly when two indexed feature maps are equal, regardless of adjacent weights and the domain on which equality is tested.
The informally defined feature relation is a genuine poset whose width is an intrinsic minimum representation size.
Small raw weight-space distance is a reliable, scale-stable surrogate for functional equivalence.
Summing incoming parameters and averaging outgoing parameters remains valid through the network's activation, bias, normalization, and residual structure.
A layer-relative threshold based on the maximum pair distance is comparable across layers and robust to outliers.
In-distribution top-1 accuracy captures all relevant functional damage from channel merging.
Test-set selection of beta does not materially bias the reported compression frontier.
Parameter reduction translates into useful latency, memory, and energy savings on target hardware.
Results from VGG and partially handled ResNet image classifiers generalize to arbitrary architectures and tasks.
Selected guided-backpropagation visualizations reliably reveal the semantics of merged channel groups.

techniques.role: Represents an architecture as a category and each concrete set of layer parameters as a functor.
Uses invertible commuting transformations between layer representations as the formal notion of functional equivalence.
Attempts to turn self-equivalences within a layer into a scalar feature-complexity measure.
Scores a channel pair using both incoming-row and outgoing-column Euclidean distances.
Repeatedly contracts the closest channel pair to obtain a narrower dense model.
Tracks merged group sizes to average downstream columns after repeated contractions.
Uses beta times the maximum pair distance as a scale-relative merge cutoff.
Tests low-loss interpolation after swapping channels judged equivalent by weight distance.
Evaluates the contracted model immediately instead of retraining or calibrating it.
Qualitatively associates selected groups of merged channels with image parts.

evaluations.setting: VGG16 trained on CIFAR-10, last-convolution and earlier-layer channel pairs
evaluations.metric: Normalized weight-distance heatmaps and test accuracy along interpolation between a checkpoint and a permuted copy
evaluations.result: The minimum reported pair distance is 2e-15, and swapping low-distance pairs causes much less interpolation damage than swapping the same number of random pairs
evaluations.baseline: Random channel permutations; no activation-equivalence oracle, independent-network comparison, or exact all-input test

evaluations.setting: VGG family trained on CIFAR-10 for 150 epochs
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy versus percentage of remaining parameters across beta values
evaluations.result: VGG16 retains 23.03% of parameters at 91.78% test accuracy versus 93.51% before merging
evaluations.baseline: Uncompressed checkpoint; beta operating points are selected using test accuracy and have no multi-seed uncertainty

evaluations.setting: VGG and ResNet variants on CIFAR-10
evaluations.metric: Remaining parameters at at least 95% of original test accuracy
evaluations.result: Larger models are reported to tolerate more merging, while ResNet18 can lose roughly 60% of parameters without a large accuracy change
evaluations.baseline: Uncompressed models of different architectures and capacities; threshold chosen on the test set

evaluations.setting: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 as a pruning method
evaluations.result: The displayed IFM curve is reported above Integral Neural Network across evaluated ratios
evaluations.baseline: INN evaluated with released code; no older data-free neuron pruning, standard structured-pruning frontier, latency, or matched hyperparameter-selection control

evaluations.setting: Torchvision VGG and ResNet checkpoints on ImageNet
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy versus percentage of remaining parameters
evaluations.result: Only about 5% of VGG parameters and 10% of ResNet50 parameters are removed before substantial degradation
evaluations.baseline: Original pretrained checkpoints; no seeds, calibration set, current compression baseline, or realized speed measurement

evaluations.setting: Torchvision ResNet50 V1 versus V2 on ImageNet
evaluations.metric: Top-1 degradation as IFM merges more channels
evaluations.result: The 80.86%-accuracy V2 checkpoint degrades faster than the 76.13%-accuracy V1 checkpoint, interpreted as greater feature diversity
evaluations.baseline: Two checkpoints trained with different recipes, leaving feature complexity confounded with optimization and preprocessing

evaluations.setting: VGG layer profiles and selected CIFAR-10 images
evaluations.metric: Estimated feature count by layer and guided-backpropagation visualizations
evaluations.result: Estimated complexity rises then falls through the network, and selected groups appear to highlight cabins, wheels, containers, legs, and boat parts
evaluations.baseline: No width-normalized, shuffled-group, alternate-attribution, annotation, or quantitative semantic baseline

evaluations.setting: One IFM merge iteration on a GeForce RTX 2080Ti
evaluations.result: Reported times range from 0.015 seconds for ResNet18 to roughly 0.8 seconds for ImageNet VGG variants
evaluations.baseline: No end-to-end compression time, inference latency, FLOPs, energy, or deployment-hardware baseline

limitations: Author-stated: IFM removes only about 5-10% of parameters on ImageNet before performance degrades, making it much less effective on harder tasks.
Author-stated: experiments cover only image classification and a small architecture family despite architecture- and data-agnostic claims.
Reviewer-identified: Proposition 3.2 substitutes the stronger LLFC premise for LMC and contains an invalid algebraic implication, breaking the claimed LMC-to-equivalence theorem.
Reviewer-identified: approximate dataset loss equality cannot by itself imply an exact categorical natural isomorphism.
Reviewer-identified: the categories, morphism equalities, feature transformations, and domain of functional equality are too underspecified for a rigorous categorical theorem.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem 3.3 does not prove both directions, and the claimed feature poset is not shown to satisfy the poset axioms.
Reviewer-identified: IFM's weight distance has no demonstrated equivalence to natural automorphisms, duplicate feature functions, poset width, or bounded output error.
Reviewer-identified: the merge rule omits biases, normalization state, nonlinear-activation conditions, residual constraints, and other architecture-specific dependencies.
Reviewer-identified: Algorithm 1 accesses a nonexistent W_(L+1), resets cluster sizes during iteration, and omits explicit tensor and dimension updates.
Reviewer-identified: beta is selected using test accuracy, introducing test leakage into the reported data-free compression workflow.
Reviewer-identified: the first-data-free-pruning claim overlooks a directly cited 2015 neuron-pruning method and is not supported by the one-baseline experiment.
Reviewer-identified: exact-equivalence language is inconsistent with nonzero accuracy losses and an explicitly approximate merging rule.
Reviewer-identified: CIFAR accuracy results lack repeated training seeds, error bars, paired tests, calibration, and out-of-distribution or robustness checks.
Reviewer-identified: the two-checkpoint ResNet50 comparison confounds feature complexity with different training recipes.
Reviewer-identified: the layer profile is not controlled for changing layer width or sensitivity to beta and weight scaling.
Reviewer-identified: semantic claims rest on selected guided-backpropagation examples without a quantitative or faithfulness evaluation.
Reviewer-identified: parameter count and per-iteration compression time do not establish inference acceleration, memory savings, or energy reduction.
Reviewer-identified: the paper does not compare with stronger modern representation-alignment or data-free folding methods that now define the field.
failure_modes: Batch-normalization scale and running statistics can make two close convolution filters functionally different or make distant raw filters equivalent after normalization.
Biases or non-positively-homogeneous activations can invalidate the sum-incoming/average-outgoing merge identity.
Residual additions require coordinated channel mappings across branches; merging only one path can create shape or semantic mismatches.
A single large-distance outlier can inflate the maximum-distance cutoff and trigger excessive merging throughout a layer.
Layerwise rescaling symmetries can arbitrarily change Euclidean weight distances while leaving the network function unchanged.
Two channels identical on CIFAR-10 test images can diverge on shifted, adversarial, rare, or continuous inputs.
Top-1 accuracy can hide large calibration, confidence, robustness, subgroup, or class-specific changes after compression.
Greedy local contractions can destroy a globally useful combination of channels even when every chosen pair looks locally close.
Repeated merges can accumulate approximation error, especially if cluster counts are reset as written in Algorithm 1.
Choosing beta on the test set can produce optimistic compression frontiers that fail on a new evaluation distribution.
Absolute feature-count profiles can merely reproduce the architecture's changing widths rather than learned intrinsic complexity.
Guided-backpropagation images can look semantically coherent even for non-causal or randomly selected features.
A smaller parameter file may not run faster when the resulting dense shapes, kernel support, or hardware alignment are unfavorable.
Natural-isomorphism claims can become vacuous if the allowed transformation class is too broad, or false if naturality is required beyond the finite dataset.
reusable_insights: Separate exact equivalence, approximate functional interchangeability, and harmless task-level compression as three distinct claims with different tests.
When invoking category theory, specify objects, morphisms, composition, component maps, and whether naturality is equality of functions or only equality on sampled activations.
Never infer an exact structural relation from approximate scalar-loss connectivity without an explicit quantitative theorem.
Audit every proof for premise substitution: empirical LLFC co-occurrence cannot silently replace an LMC hypothesis.
Validate a feature-redundancy metric against synthetic networks with known duplicate, scaled, permuted, dead, and distribution-specific neurons.
Canonicalize layerwise rescaling and normalization before using Euclidean weight distance as a similarity signal.
Derive merge rules separately for linear, ReLU, biased, normalized, convolutional, residual, grouped, and attention blocks.
Tune compression thresholds on a validation set or predeclare a resource target; preserve the test set for one final comparison.
Report the complete Pareto frontier over accuracy, calibration, robustness, latency, memory, energy, and parameter count.
Use multiple seeds and paired per-example or per-class tests to distinguish compression noise from systematic functional damage.
Normalize layer-complexity profiles by width and test stability across thresholds, parameter symmetries, and alternative similarity measures.
Use causal ablation, concept annotations, random-group controls, and multiple attribution methods before assigning semantics to channel groups.
Compare against historical data-free neuron merging as well as modern folding, pruning, and low-rank baselines before making priority claims.
Release a reference implementation whose tensor updates and supported architecture contracts match the pseudocode exactly.
open_questions: What restricted categorical construction yields a non-vacuous, checkable equivalence notion for finite neural networks?
Under what additional assumptions, if any, can exact LLFC imply a natural isomorphism between parameterized layer maps?
Can one construct a simple counterexample benchmark that separates LMC, LLFC, model stitching, representational similarity, and true functional equivalence?
How should duplicate feature indices be quotiented so that the proposed relation is a genuine poset and its width has an operational meaning?
Can feature complexity be defined as a minimum sufficient internal dimension with approximation and generalization guarantees?
Can a scale- and normalization-invariant weight metric predict output perturbation without calibration data?
What is the exact loss-preserving merge operator for biased ReLU-BN blocks and for residual or attention architectures?
Does IFM remain competitive with model folding and projection-based compression at matched compression, latency, and no-data constraints?
How stable are selected merge groups across seeds, datasets, augmentations, checkpoints, and adversarial distribution shifts?
Do estimated feature-complexity profiles predict generalization after controlling for architecture width, training recipe, and weight scale?
Are the visualized semantic groups causally necessary and sufficient for the claimed concepts, or merely correlated saliency patterns?
Can a compression certificate bound worst-case or distributional output change after a sequence of greedy merges?
What stopping rule can be fixed without labeled validation data while remaining robust to distance outliers?
When does parameter reduction translate into actual speed or energy gains on accelerators with aligned dense kernels?

competitive_landscape.title: Data-free parameter pruning for Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Srinivas and Babu already remove similar neurons from a trained network without training data, reporting large fully connected-layer reductions. It is narrower and older than IFM's convolutional experiments, but directly undercuts the manuscript's broad claim to be the first pruning method needing neither data nor fine-tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Similarity and Matching of Neural Network Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Dr. Frankenstein tests whether one network can use another's representation through learned affine stitching and explicitly distinguishes functional from statistical similarity. IFM is data-free and intra-network, but its weight-distance proxy lacks the task-grounded interchangeability test that stitching provides.

competitive_landscape.title: Grounding Representation Similarity Through Statistical Testing
competitive_landscape.difference: Ding, Denain, and Steinhardt require similarity measures to be sensitive to function-changing perturbations and specific to function-preserving ones, revealing failures across popular metrics. That controlled validation framework is exactly what IFM's proposed feature complexity and weight distance lack.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Symmetries of Deep Learning Models and their Internal Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Godfrey et al. derive architecture- and nonlinearity-dependent intertwiner groups that preserve the represented function while changing internal states. This supplies a more explicit algebraic account of allowable equivalences than IFM's underspecified natural transformations and highlights why raw Euclidean weight distance is not symmetry invariant.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: Git Re-Basin explicitly aligns independently trained models modulo hidden-unit permutations and studies when interpolation barriers disappear, including counterexamples. IFM borrows incoming/outgoing weight matching but uses it to contract channels inside one model; Git Re-Basin does not support the stronger inference that LMC itself proves exact feature equivalence.

competitive_landscape.title: Going Beyond Linear Mode Connectivity: The Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity
competitive_landscape.difference: LLFC is a stronger, approximate layerwise property empirically observed in nearly all layers when selected models exhibit LMC. The reviewed paper treats exact LLFC as if it followed definitionally from LMC inside Proposition 3.2's proof, exceeding what this primary source establishes.

competitive_landscape.title: Exploring the Complexity of Deep Neural Networks through Functional Equivalence
competitive_landscape.difference: Shen studies equivalence classes of parameterizations to derive a covering-number bound and an effective-parameter-space account of optimization. It offers a quantitative learning-theory notion of complexity, whereas IFM proposes a layer-wise poset width and an empirical compression proxy without a bound connecting the two.

competitive_landscape.title: Latent Functional Maps: a spectral framework for representation alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: Latent Functional Maps aligns low-dimensional representation manifolds in a spectral functional basis and validates comparison, correspondence, transfer, stitching, retrieval, and multiple modalities. IFM is simpler and data-free but covers only same-model channel contraction and supplies far less evidence for intrinsic alignment or semantics.

competitive_landscape.title: Forget the Data and Fine-Tuning! Just Fold the Network to Compress
competitive_landscape.difference: Model folding clusters structurally similar neurons, adds explicit variance-preservation repairs, benchmarks IFM directly, and extends no-data/no-fine-tuning compression to ResNet18 and LLaMA-7B with stronger high-compression results. It operationalizes the same broad idea while addressing variance collapse and scaling beyond the reviewed experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: Functional Alignment Can Mislead: Examining Model Stitching
competitive_landscape.difference: Smith, Mannering, and Marcu show that representations encoding different biases, tasks, modalities, or even clustered random noise can still be functionally stitched. This warns that preserved downstream accuracy is insufficient evidence that IFM groups intrinsically equivalent or semantically identical features.

competitive_landscape.title: Cut Less, Fold More: Model Compression through the Lens of Projection Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: This follow-on formalizes pruning and folding as orthogonal projections, derives reconstruction and functional-perturbation comparisons, and evaluates more than one thousand checkpoints across CNNs, ViTs, and CLIP. It supplies the kind of error geometry, architecture breadth, and replicated evaluation absent from IFM's poset-based account.

competitive_landscape.title: Grounding Functional Similarity by Invariance-Aware Model Stitching
competitive_landscape.difference: Athanasiadis, Karmush, and Felsberg add backward/invariance compatibility because standard forward stitching can overstate similarity, and test multiple architectures and datasets with three seeds. Their criterion reinforces that IFM's accuracy-preserving merges do not by themselves demonstrate shared invariances or intrinsic functional equivalence.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICML 2026 accepted regular version, last modified 2026-06-24

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first formal category-theoretic definition of functionally equivalent neural features, an intrinsic layer-wise feature-complexity metric, a proof that LMC suffices for equivalence, and the first data-agnostic pruning method requiring neither training manipulation nor fine-tuning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines network-as-functor language, natural transformations, an attempted poset-width definition, a bidirectional weight-matching distance, and greedy channel contraction, then reports no-fine-tuning CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments plus layer and semantic visualizations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The practically reusable novelty is the simple incoming-plus-outgoing weight heuristic for dense post-training channel merging and its empirical demonstration across VGG and limited ResNet settings. The stronger novelty claims do not survive audit: Proposition 3.2 substitutes LLFC for LMC and makes an invalid inference, Theorem 3.3 and the poset are incomplete, IFM is not linked to the formal metric, and prior data-free neuron pruning predates the priority claim. Subsequent model-folding work provides a more complete and scalable version of the compression idea.

reviewer_notes: Read all 19 extracted pages, including references, Algorithm 1, both proof appendices, experiment details, runtime table, distance heatmaps, and guided-backpropagation appendix. The cached artifact is the current arXiv v2 dated 2023-11-26 and still bears a preprint header; this review assesses that exact hashed text rather than silently replacing it with the later ICLR 2024 proceedings PDF. Twelve primary-source competitors were checked through arXiv, OpenReview, PMLR, and official NeurIPS proceedings as of 2026-08-23. Highest-severity audit result: the LMC-to-natural-isomorphism proposition is unsupported twice over—its proof assumes LLFC, and its derived bilinear identity does not imply the claimed cross-network layer equality. A helper-agent spawn was attempted for independent audit but the global thread pool was full, so all mathematical and empirical checks here were performed directly.
